title: Announcement channels: an x channel, a broadcast recipient class and a cost on deliveries
description:
Papyrus needs Caducus to post announcements to a publication's own X (Twitter) account, as part of Ryan's one-notification-system decision (Papyrus PPY-824c14). Papyrus epic: AnthusAI/Papyrus PPY-09ee86 "Scheduled publishing and automated announcements"; Papyrus story PPY-9f4d66 waits on this. Design: Papyrus docs/plans/scheduled-publishing-and-announcements.md (PR AnthusAI/Papyrus#1459).

Goal: three small additions, released in one Caducus version, so a host can deliver a kind to a site's connected public account and record what it cost.

1. **`x` channel** (`caducus.notify.channels.x`), a `Channel` like `email`: `send` creates a post (POST https://api.x.com/2/tweets, OAuth 2.0 user token) and returns `Outcome(status="sent", provider_message_id=<post id>)`; `delete(provider_message_id)` deletes it (DELETE /2/tweets/:id); `find_recent(text_or_url)` reads the account's latest posts so an unknown outcome (timeout, 5xx) is resolved before any retry, because X documents no idempotency key. Rate limits: wait until `x-rate-limit-reset`. Escapes nothing that X would turn into a mention unless the text already has it. Tokens come from a **token provider** the host passes in (Papyrus stores the rotating refresh token in SSM SecureString and refreshes under its own lock); the channel never stores or logs tokens.
2. **`broadcast` recipient class**: the recipient is a site's connected channel account (`CHANNELACCT#<channel>#<accountId>`), not a Person; no consent, preference or suppression applies; routing sends a broadcast kind only to the accounts the host names for it. Dedupe on `eventId` as today (Papyrus sends `story.announce:<accountId>:<lineageId>`).
3. **`cost` on deliveries**: an optional `cost` (decimal string) and `costCurrency` on the delivery log, set by channels that charge per request (X: post with link $0.200, delete $0.010, read $0.005 per docs.x.com pricing, 2026-11-12; the host passes prices as configuration, never constants in code). Never moves backward, like status.

```gherkin
Feature: A host announces on a publication's X account through Caducus
  A publication posts each qualifying Story to its own X account once, and the
  host can see the post and what it cost.

  Scenario: A broadcast kind is posted once
    Given a host that connected the X account "@example_pub" as a broadcast recipient
    When it sends the event "story.announce:acct1:lineage9" twice
    Then exactly one post is made
    And the delivery records the post id and a cost of 0.200 USD

  Scenario: An unknown outcome is checked before retrying
    Given the post request timed out
    When the delivery is retried
    Then the account's recent posts are read first
    And if the post is there the delivery is marked sent without posting again

  Scenario: X asks us to wait
    Given X answers 429 with a reset time
    Then the delivery waits until that time and then posts

  Scenario: A broadcast ignores reader preferences
    Given a broadcast kind
    Then no consent, preference or suppression lookup is made for it

  Scenario: Deleting a post records its cost
    When the host deletes a delivered post
    Then the post is deleted at X
    And the delivery shows it was withdrawn and adds the delete cost

  Scenario: Tokens never appear in the log
    Given any delivery on the X channel
    Then no token appears in the delivery log or in the function's logs
```

Open questions: whether `find_recent` should match on the link (preferred: UTM-tagged canonical link is unique per Story) or the exact text.
